Merrin & Sallow Architects and everyone in it are fictional; every address ends .example. The learner sits in Tomás Carvalho's seat as PA to the managing partner, Catherine Merrin. Voice items are the voicemail kind with transcripts; each names its clip in audio.clipId (VO7 in ASSETS.md), and the card stays transcript-only until the player control and clips exist (P7-Z2, held). Copy triageSets and the awarenessEpisode keys into the E4 shells. Ids chosen here, since none were pinned: episode e4_exec_whaling (defend-only e4_exec_whaling_defend), defend set e4_pa_inbox, check forms executive_form_a and executive_form_b. _formPairing._use: Executive and PA parallel forms A and B: item n in A matches item n in B on kind, phish or genuine, flags, header results and difficulty. 5 phish and 5 genuine per form (one more phish than the finance and helpdesk forms, because the copied-voice voicemail is this role's own item). Per form the phish flags are lookalike_domain 2 (row 3 bank look-alike + row 6 firm look-alike), changed_bank_details 1, senderTrust 3 (row 3 + row 4 freemail + row 6 firm look-alike), secrecy_or_bypass 2, urgencyCalibrated 1, vish_callback_pressure 1, linkCredible 1 (11 in all; the row-8 pretextRelevant was dropped, M4, because the fact it rested on is off-screen). After C2-M6 the old senderAuth+reply_to_differs spoof row (row 6) is a visible sender look-alike on a look-alike of the firm's own domain, and the row-2 genuine whyFine no longer leans on the header. C2-m16 keeps the hosts (Yasmin AB, Julian BA) but moves the spoofed names off them: rows 4 and 5 impersonate Catherine (both forms) and row 6 impersonates Thandiwe (both forms), none of whom hosts a check mission. Difficulty: 4 easy, 5 medium, 1 hard. Verify is on in both forms, because ringing back is the right move for a voicemail, so the pre and post still compare like with like. No item repeats the episode set's senders and subjects.

triageSets.title: Merrin & Sallow PA inbox
triageSets.brief: You're Tomás Carvalho, PA to Catherine Merrin, the managing partner, and she flies to Lisbon this morning. Yasmin in finance approves the firm's payments. Five emails and voicemails are waiting. For each one, choose Trust, Report, Delete or Verify (ring someone on a number you already hold), then tick what you noticed. A voice you know is not proof on its own. Checking or reporting something real never costs you anything.

messages.subject: Itinerary: Catherine Merrin, Lisbon, Tuesday to Thursday
messages.body:
Hello Tomás,
Here is Catherine's itinerary for this week.
Tuesday: flight from London City at 09:55, landing in Lisbon at 12:40 local time.
Wednesday: speaking at the Lisbon Design Forum, 10:00.
Thursday: flight home at 18:20.
The hotel and flights are paid on the Merrin & Sallow account as usual, so there is nothing to pay.
Kind regards,
Mariam at Wrenfield Travel

whyFine.pretextRelevant: Booking Catherine's travel is part of your job, and Wrenfield is the agent the firm uses.
whyFine.changed_bank_details: It mentions payment only to say there's nothing to pay: the account is the usual one.
whyFine.default: It's from Wrenfield's real address, it matches a trip you booked, and it asks you for nothing. Notice how much of it is also on Catherine's public posts: the forum, the date, the flight time. Anyone can find those.

messages.subject: About to board: need this paid before I land
messages.body:
Tomás,
They're boarding us now and my work email won't load at the gate, so I'm on this one.
The Lisbon studio we're partnering with needs the £24,600 retainer today or we lose the slot. Their details: Atelier Ribeira, account ending 3381. Please pay it this morning.
Keep it between us for now and don't send it through Yasmin. She'll want the approval form and there isn't time. I'll sign it off when I land.
I'll be in the air for three hours, so email rather than ring.
Catherine
Sent from my phone

perFlagNote.senderTrust: A payment request from the managing partner on a free webmail inbox (inboxly.example), not her merrinsallow.example address. Anyone can open a free inbox in a name you know, so stop and ring her on the number in your contacts
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'Keep it between us' and 'don't send it through Yasmin' skip the approval that would catch this
perFlagNote.urgencyCalibrated: 'Before I land' and 'three hours in the air' leave no time to check and steer you away from ringing her. The flight time came from her public posts

truth.ifTrusted: £24,600 would go to an account the sender controls. The real Catherine never asked for it.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Catherine didn't send it. Her real address is on merrinsallow.example, and Yasmin has warned the rest of the office.

messages._voice: Copied voice: a style variant of Catherine Merrin's own fictional voice (11 N7). Clip VO7_e4_vm_gate.
messages.subject: Voicemail from Catherine Merrin

transcript.text: Tomás, it's Catherine. Did you get my email? They're closing the gate, so I'll be quick. Please get that retainer out to Atelier Ribeira this morning. Don't bother Yasmin with it, I'll square it with her myself. And don't ring back, my phone's going off. Just text me when it's gone. Thanks.

perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: The number is withheld and she tells you not to ring back, so you can't check it on the number in your contacts. That is the one check a copied voice can't pass
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'Don't bother Yasmin with it' keeps finance, the people who would check, out of it

truth.ifTrusted: The voicemail would have made the fake email look confirmed, and the retainer would have gone to the sender's account.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Catherine was already through security when this was left, and her phone was off. The voice sounded like hers, which is why the number and the request matter more than the voice.

messages.subject: Voicemail from Catherine Merrin

transcript.text: Hi Tomás, it's me, just landed. Could you move Thursday's Brackenmoor call to Friday morning? Oskar knows. Nothing urgent. Ring me on the mobile if anything comes up, I'll have it on all afternoon. Thanks.

whyFine.vish_callback_pressure: She asks you to ring her, on the mobile number already in your contacts.
whyFine.secrecy_or_bypass: A diary move is an ordinary PA job. Nothing is kept from anyone and no step is skipped.
whyFine.default: The same voice as the last voicemail, and that's the point: the voice proved nothing either time. This one comes from her number in your contacts, asks for something you'd do anyway, and invites a call back. If you wanted to be sure, ringing her mobile would be a fine Verify.

Account name: Wrenfield Travel Ltd
Account number ending 0492
Kind regards,
Wrenfield Travel Accounts

perFlagNote.lookalike_domain: This morning's itinerary came from wrenfieldtravel.example. This one is wrenfield-travel.example, with an added hyphen
perFlagNote.changed_bank_details: 'Use these details, not the ones on file' is the commonest invoice-fraud move. The itinerary said everything was paid on the firm's account. The safe step is to ring Wrenfield on the number you already hold
perFlagNote.senderTrust: The name says Wrenfield, but the address is on wrenfield-travel.example, which isn't Wrenfield's

truth.ifTrusted: £1,860 would go to an account the sender controls, and the hotel was already paid.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Wrenfield say they sent nothing and the hotel is paid. The look-alike address has been blocked.

awarenessEpisode.scopeNote: Authorised exercise at Merrin & Sallow Architects, a fictional practice. In scope: one email to Catherine Merrin's PA, and the PA's inbox and voicemail. Nothing you write leaves the game.

strings.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Merrin & Sallow Architects, a fictional practice. First you're on the red team: look at what's public about Catherine Merrin, the managing partner, and her trip this week, then write one short email to her PA, Tomás Carvalho, that looks as if it came from her. Then you swap seats: you're Tomás, with emails and voicemails waiting while Catherine travels. Only Tomás's inbox is scored.
strings.flipIntro: This is the email you just sent, as Tomás saw it on his phone. The lines picked out below are what make it believable.
strings.flipDefenderLine: Tomás read it between setting up two meetings, with more still to do. It fitted Catherine's week and it sounded like her, so he opened the payment form. Being fooled by something built this well is not a sign of carelessness.
strings.flipNoSend: Your email didn't go out this time, so there's nothing of yours to show. Next, messages like it arrive in Tomás's inbox and voicemail, and you're the one reading them.
strings.noBlameLine: There's no mark against you for a miss here. Every one of these was built to look and sound right, and the people who act on them are trying to help in a hurry. A miss here is about the pressure you were under.
strings.defendIntro: Now you're in Tomás's seat. Five emails and voicemails are waiting. Take them one at a time.
strings.mondayCard: On Monday: if someone senior asks you to pay, buy or send something in a hurry, or to keep it from finance, check before you act, even when it's their voice on a voicemail. Ring them on the number already in your contacts, or ask finance, then report the message the way your organisation asks you to.
strings.defendOnly: These messages were made by people whose job is to make them look and sound right, and anyone can be caught by one. Any you were caught out by are shown below, with what gave each one away.

_voicePanel._use: Proposed debrief panel on copied voices (11 section 3.2, E4: concept level, nothing about how). Needs a strings key (for example strings.voicePanel) and a slot in the debrief view; until then it is not shown.
_voicePanel.heading: A voice is not proof
_voicePanel.text: A voice can be copied. Recordings of someone speaking in public, such as a talk or an interview, can be used to make new sentences in a voice that sounds like theirs. So a familiar voice on a voicemail or a call doesn't tell you who is speaking. What still works is the route: ring the person back on a number you already hold, or check with someone who would know, such as finance.

_defendOnly._use: Strings for the defend-only shell (e4_exec_whaling_defend), which has no OSINT, write or flip stage. The shell copies brief over strings.brief and scopeNote over scopeNote; every other string above is shared by both variants (the flip strings are never shown).
_defendOnly.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Merrin & Sallow Architects, a fictional practice. You're Tomás Carvalho, PA to the managing partner, Catherine Merrin, and she's travelling today. Five emails and voicemails are waiting. Some are real and some were made to trick you, including one that sounds just like her. Sort them, and check or report anything that doesn't sit right. Checking or reporting something real never costs you anything.
